page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512 vector instructions and AES cryptography. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

For storage and networking, the m5dn.xlarge includes a bundled 150 GB local NVMe SSD instance store. It delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps and is optimized for both network and Elastic Block Store (EBS) performance. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates modest compute capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance falling into the bottom 25%. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores reflect weak performance relative to newer hardware generations.

Memory performance is mixed; while the Passmark memory score ranks in the average tier, large-block memory read and write bandwidth benchmarks show weaker throughput. Database operations, such as Redis SET operations and Passmark database tests, also register in the lower performance tier. Given its hardware profile, this instance offers a qualitative balance of local NVMe storage and dedicated compute resources, making it suitable for general-purpose workloads, moderate web serving, and development environments that require fast local scratch space without demanding high-intensity CPU throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services m5dn.xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 4 vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and a 3.1 GHz clock speed. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory and a bundled 150 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed instance storage. Operating on an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps and is optimized for EBS and network throughput. Benchmark results indicate modest compute and memory performance, with CPU and database operations generally placing in the lower tiers, though memory subsystem benchmarks achieve average ratings. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring a balance of dedicated compute, moderate memory, and fast local storage, such as general-purpose web serving, development environments, and basic database tasks.
